_comment: Permissions policy for the FDE gate service Lambda execution role. Note what is NOT here: any database authorization. This policy only gets the function to a place where it CAN open a Postgres connection (read the secret, or mint an IAM DB auth token); what that connection may then do is decided entirely at the SQL layer by SET LOCAL ROLE fde_gate_service / fde_prodops (see fde_mcp/db.py and db/010_roles_and_seed_policy.sql). An operator widening this policy does not widen what the service can do to the graph -- that is the point of putting the boundary in Postgres. Replace ${AWS_REGION}, ${AWS_ACCOUNT_ID}, ${FDE_DB_SECRET_ARN}, ${DB_RESOURCE_ID} and ${FDE_GATE_FUNCTION_NAME} at deploy time.

Statement._comment: IAM database authentication, the alternative to the secret. Scoped to the two dbuser names this service ever connects as. It connects as an owner-adjacent principal and downgrades per request, so these are the LOGIN roles, not the SET LOCAL ROLE targets.
Agent steps in a workflow run. Scoped to runtimes named fde-* so this role cannot invoke an arbitrary agent runtime someone else deployed in the same account.
The async self-invoke that keeps a slow agent/tool step off the 29-second API Gateway budget. Scoped to this function's own ARN: it may re-invoke itself and nothing else.

Only needed when the database is not publicly reachable, which is the normal case. Required by Lambda to create and clean up the ENIs it uses to reach a VPC; the actions cannot be resource-scoped (AWS does not support it for these), which is why they are isolated in their own statement rather than hidden among the scoped ones.
